properties.evidence: Applies to OPTION (c) ONLY, and is drawn so the conflict cannot be missed if (c) is ever picked up. The source document proposes reflow2 'refuse to accept a passing verification that has never recorded a failing run' — a refusal is reflow2 validating a check rather than recording a claim, which is exactly what this accepted non-goal forbids. Options (a) and (b) do NOT conflict: recording what the author says a check was observed to do is the same class of instrument as provenance and the drift dispositions. Picking (c) means overturning this non-goal deliberately, not working around it.
